title: Canary rollback orchestration & escalation playbook for rollout regressions
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Summary: After two recent customer escalations tied to model rollout regressions (hosted: INC-2026-0310-A, dedicated: INC-2026-0312-B, private: customer-reported on-prem failure), we need a cross-environment orchestration and escalation playbook that standardizes detection, canary criteria, automatic/manual rollback triggers, and customer communication templates. Goal: reduce mean time to mitigation for rollout regressions from hours to <30 minutes for hosted, and provide clear SLAs and runbook steps for Dedicated and Private customers so we can coordinate faster with customers and support teams.

Scope: This ticket covers creation of the playbook, automation hooks for the serving control plane, telemetry/alert thresholds, and templates for support/SRE-run actions. Implementation touches: serving runtime routing, console rollback UI, dedicated capacity operator workflows, private upgrade/rollback procedures, and Support/CS escalation flows.

Problem statement: Current rollouts can silently introduce quality regressions or latency/instability in production. Existing canary policies are inconsistent across environments: hosted rollbacks are manual and slow when not auto-flagged, dedicated customers sometimes have pinned model versions which complicates rollback coordination, and private deployments require customer consent for on-prem changes. We observed two failure modes in March incidents: 1) model-level quality regression (increased hallucinations on a known eval set) and 2) runtime regression (latency spikes due to kernel selection changes). Both manifested during canary windows but were undetected or lacked automated rollback.

Requirements and constraints:
- Provide a single canonical playbook that differentiates actions by environment (hosted / dedicated / private).
- Define canary metrics (example: token error rate, top-1 mismatch on golden prompts, 95th percentile latency increase relative to baseline, request fail rate) with explicit thresholds.
- Implement automatic rollback for hosted when OOMs/failure-rate or quality delta exceed thresholds for >2m.
- Define manual rollback flow for Dedicated with customer-notify and operator approval steps; when customer pins prevent immediate rollback, provide fast-fallback to compatible variant and document timeline.
- For Private, provide standardized guidance and pre-built rollback artifacts (model binary, config delta, step-by-step restore), and a customer communication template with expected time-to-restore.
- Integrate with Console: surface canary health, allow one-click rollback for hosted and operator-initiated rollback for Dedicated.
- Ensure telemetry hooks into console observability dashboards and Support incident workspace (links to traces, perf histograms, recent model diffs, and failed request samples).

Deliverables:
- Canonical rollback playbook document (Confluence) with decision tree per environment.
- Automation PRs in serving control plane to trigger rollback hooks and emit standardized incident events.
- Console UX changes: canary health card + rollback button (hosted), operator rollback workflow for Dedicated.
- Dedicated customer runbook templates and Private on-prem rollback bundle.
- Support/CS escalation email/snippet templates and SLAs.
- Post-implementation test harness: synthetic canary tests that simulate quality/latency regressions and validate correct automated/manual rollback behavior.

Success metrics:
- Hosted mean time to mitigation for rollout regressions reduced to <30 minutes (target).
- 90% of Dedicated customer rollbacks initiated within 1 hour of verified regression.
- Private deployment playbook accepted by 3 pilot customers and tested end-to-end.

Risks and mitigation:
- False positives triggering unnecessary rollback => require dual-signal checks (perf + quality test) and a short confirmation window to avoid flapping.
- Rollback may not be compatible with downstream schema changes => include compatibility checks and preflight validation.
- Customer coordination delays for Private => pre-obtain emergency rollback consent for high-SLA customers where possible.
acceptance_criteria: Confluence playbook published and reviewed by SRE, Runtime, Support, and PM
Serving control plane emits canary incident events and can trigger automated hosted rollback via API
Console displays canary health and provides rollback button for hosted rollouts
Dedicated rollback workflow documented and validated with at least two dedicated customers in staging
Private rollback bundle (binary + steps) created and tested with one pilot customer
Synthetic canary tests executed in CI that inject quality and latency regressions and verify rollback behavior
steps_to_reproduce: Deploy model variant X to canary (10% traffic) with compiled kernel set K2
Run golden prompt set and note reference metrics (baseline precision, latency p95)
Expand canary to 25% but inject a regression (swap to K3 or introduce quantization flag change)
Observe canary metrics: quality delta > 5% mismatch on golden set, p95 latency +80ms, error-rate jump >3%
Verify automation triggers and operator notifications (or lack thereof)
mitigations: Hotfix: revert model binary and kernel selection to previous compatible revision for hosted via control-plane rollback API
Fallback: route affected traffic to stable model variant or regional fallback pool
Support action: open dedicated incident workspace, notify customer success/AE, and run guided checklist
Postmortem: collect traces, failed request samples, and golden-set deltas for RCA

notes: Operational nuance: For Dedicated customers that have pinning enabled, plan includes a 'fast-fallback' which switches canary traffic to a compatible variant automatically while we negotiate a full rollback with the customer. For Private customers, provide an encrypted rollback bundle and an optional remote-assist workflow only with explicit customer authorization.
